Closest precedents are pairwise sequential rules and directed item-kNN: aggregate item-to-item association scores from recent history. Positive clipped log-transition lift is a popularity-corrected transition statistic, resembling positive PMI when probabilities share a consistent sampling definition; five-item aggregation does not itself imply five-way association rules. Compare sequential-rule counts/confidence, lift-weighted rules, and co-occurrence/cosine item-kNN ([baseline implementations](https://github.com/saraLatifi/session-rec)). [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152) is the closest learned structural analogue, combining long-term item similarity with higher-order Markov transitions; its learned factorization differs from a fixed transition table added to SASRec.

Recommended controls: identical SASRec checkpoint with residual disabled; frozen checkpoint plus validation-tuned fixed amplitude; frozen checkpoint with BCE-trained amplitude; jointly trained SASRec plus amplitude; matched continued SASRec training without residual. Keep transition tables training-only, candidate sets and search budgets matched, and select using macro validation HR@10. Include transition-only scoring, last-item versus five-item aggregation, and confidence versus lift ablations. These distinguish post-hoc score fusion from gains requiring backbone adaptation.

Analytically, for z=s+αr and α=sigmoid(a), ∂L/∂a=(sigmoid(z)−y)rα(1−α). Initial α=0.01 implies a≈−4.595 and multiplier 0.0099. Correctly saturated predictions add another near-zero factor; incorrectly saturated predictions retain substantial BCE logit gradients, though the amplitude gate still attenuates them. This follows from the documented [BCE-with-logits objective](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss.html). Small gradients do not necessarily imply proportionally small Adam updates. Nevertheless, learning reliable ranking improvements is not guaranteed: BCE optimizes sampled classification, and residual magnitude and candidate score gaps determine whether 0.01 changes rankings. A frozen-checkpoint amplitude sweep directly tests usefulness without relying on gate learning.
